title: One Lakh Tickets Sold, One Month to Go: India Is Already Losing Its Mind Over Spider-Man
excerpt: Tom Holland's 'Brand New Day' hasn't released yet — but its advance booking is already rewriting Hollywood records in India, and we're getting it before America
body:
A month before a single frame flickers on an IMAX screen, Spider-Man: Brand New Day has already made history in India. The advance booking for Tom Holland's return as Peter Parker has crossed 1 lakh tickets in PVR INOX alone — a number that, for context, most Bollywood films would be thrilled to hit in their entire first week.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=62bIsvRcPv0

And the film doesn't release until July 30.

The trajectory has been staggering. When bookings opened on June 19, the film sold 45,000 tickets in its first 24 hours — almost entirely premium-format and 4DX screenings. Within six days, that number had doubled and then some, blasting past the 1 lakh mark in national multiplex chains, with Cinepolis and independent screens piling on. Additional shows are being added across metros and tier-2 cities to meet demand that shows zero sign of peaking.

This is the same Spider-Man franchise that opened to approximately ₹40 crore gross in India with No Way Home in 2021 — one of the biggest Hollywood openings the country has ever seen. Trade analysts are now saying Brand New Day is tracking to match or exceed that number.

And here's the detail the diaspora should love: India gets it first. The film releases July 30 in Indian cinemas — a full day before its July 31 debut in North America. For a country that was historically treated as an afterthought in Hollywood release strategies, that scheduling flip isn't just logistics — it's recognition of how much India moves the needle on global box office.

The film's trailer became the first in history to cross 1 billion views — a milestone that even Avengers: Endgame never reached.

The cast is a large part of the pull. Tom Holland returns as Peter Parker navigating a post-No Way Home world where nobody remembers who he is — existentially devastating for a superhero who built his identity on being the friendly neighbourhood guy. Zendaya is back as MJ, alongside Jacob Batalon as Ned, Jon Bernthal in what's rumoured to be a pivotal role, Mark Ruffalo reprising Bruce Banner, and Sadie Sink making her MCU debut.

Director Destin Daniel Cretton, who brought unexpected emotional weight to Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, is reportedly steering this instalment toward a more grounded, character-driven tone — less multiverse spectacle, more personal stakes. The early marketing certainly suggests a Spider-Man who's fighting for connection, not just survival.

For Indian audiences, the film will release in English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada — casting the widest possible net across language markets. The Hindi dubbed version, in particular, has historically driven massive single-screen numbers. No Way Home's Hindi version alone accounted for a significant chunk of its Indian gross, pulling audiences well beyond the traditional English-language multiplex crowd into small-town single screens. Brand New Day looks ready to push that penetration even deeper.

What the numbers suggest: If Brand New Day crosses ₹40 crore gross on opening day in India, it would become the biggest Hollywood opening the country has ever seen. Given the advance booking pace — 1 lakh tickets in a single chain with five weeks still to go — that target looks not just achievable but conservative. Globally, the film is projected for a $200 million opening weekend in North America, which would make it one of the biggest releases of the year, period.

For NRI audiences in the US, UK, and Canada, there's a bittersweet twist: India's July 30 release means spoilers will be live on desi social media a full day before you can see it stateside. Consider this your warning to mute your WhatsApp groups.

Cocktail 2, which crossed the ₹1 million admissions milestone this week, and Welcome To The Jungle, currently tearing through its opening weekend, have proven that Indian audiences are showing up when the product is right. If Spider-Man's advance numbers are any indication, July 30 could make June's crowded calendar look quaint.

Mark the date. Book your IMAX seats. This one's going to fill up long before the popcorn machine is warm.
